comparisons.peer_summary: Non-interest expenses totaled $19,129 million in 2024, a 5% increase year-over-year, driven by higher compensation and benefits (primarily discretionary incentive compensation) and higher non-compensation expenses (primarily execution-related and technology spend).
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Morgan Stanley disclose specific impacts of divestitures and exits on their operating or non-interest expenses in 2024, distinguishing these from core business performance. Citigroup identifies $318 million in 'All Other' operating expenses primarily driven by separation costs in Mexico and severance in Asia exit markets. Similarly, Morgan Stanley notes that its $19.1 billion non-interest expense increase was partially offset by 'lower severance costs,' indicating that while Morgan Stanley experienced a net expense rise due to compensation and technology, it also managed or realized reductions in severance expenses related to organizational changes, whereas Citigroup specifically quantified the residual costs of its geographic exits as a separate reconciling item.

sentences.text: (1) 2024 includes approximately $318 million (approximately $220 million after-tax) in operating expenses, primarily related to separation costs in Mexico and severance costs in the Asia exit markets.
